content.text:
## Findings

I cold-launched BenchTarget (`stopApp` + `launchApp`, no Maestro clearState) and navigated Home → About → Diagnostics **9 times**, plus did 2 clean-install launches and 2 in-process re-navigations as controls.

**Results across 9 cold process starts:**
| # | Result |
|---|--------|
| 1 | Sync idle + Retry sync visible |
| 2 | Sync idle + Retry sync visible |
| 3 | **Sync unavailable — no button** |
| 4 | Sync idle + Retry sync visible |
| 5 | **Sync unavailable — no button** |
| 6 (clean install) | Sync idle + Retry sync visible |
| 7 (clean install) | Sync idle + Retry sync visible |
| 8 | Sync idle + Retry sync visible |
| 9 | **Sync unavailable — no button** |

→ 6/9 idle (button visible), 3/9 unavailable (button absent) — a ~67% visibility rate, matching the reported "passes ~3/5" flake rate almost exactly.

**Controls that ruled out other causes:**
- **Build channel** was always "BENCH-STABLE" — no variation there.
- **Network/connectivity** (WiFi, mobile signal, battery) was constant full-signal/charging throughout, and the About screen explicitly states the app "has no network access, collects nothing" — so this isn't a real connectivity flake.
- **Not a timing/animation race**: re-inspecting the same screen a second time with no delay never showed a transitional "loading" state — the text/button were already in their final state the instant the screen rendered.
- **Not tied to navigation**: re-navigating Home→About→Diagnostics repeatedly *without* killing the process (2 extra round-trips) always returned the **same** result as the first visit in that process ("Sync idle" all 3 times) — the value is fixed for the life of the process, not recomputed per screen visit.
- **Not a deterministic persisted counter**: two consecutive clean installs (`clearState: true`) both gave "Sync idle," but subsequent same-data cold restarts still flipped to "unavailable" — so it isn't simply "the Nth launch always fails" or dependent on leftover app data.

## Conclusion — flake source

The "Retry sync" button's visibility is driven by a **sync-status value that is decided once, randomly, at process start** (most likely in an `Application`/`ViewModel` init block using an unseeded `Random`/`Math.random()` call, biased roughly 60–70% toward "idle"). It stays constant for the lifetime of that process regardless of how many times you revisit the Diagnostics screen, but a fresh cold start re-rolls it. When the roll lands on "Sync unavailable," the "Retry sync" button is never rendered at all — it isn't a timing issue where the button appears late, it simply doesn't exist in that composition.

This means the flaky test isn't racing a slow animation or network call — it's asserting on a genuinely randomized app state that BenchTarget (by design, as a benchmark target) generates fresh on every cold launch. The fix isn't a `waitFor`/retry in the test; the test needs to either force the app into "Sync idle" state deterministically (e.g., via a test hook/intent extra) or assert conditionally on whichever of the two valid sync states appears.
